schema_notes.category: one of: factual | synthesis | contradiction | timeline | adversarial
schema_notes.question: the question text
schema_notes.answer: your hand-verified correct answer, written in your own words

supporting_evidence.paper_id: arXiv id or short citation key, e.g. arXiv:2210.17323
supporting_evidence.passage: the exact sentence(s) or a close paraphrase of the passage that supports the answer -- this is what you'll check retrieval against later

schema_notes.notes: optional: anything tricky about this question (e.g. answer depends on model size, or two papers use different definitions)

questions.question: What bit-width does GPTQ quantize model weights to in its main reported experiments?
questions.answer: GPTQ is primarily evaluated at 3-bit and 4-bit weight quantization, applied post-training without retraining.

questions.question: What are the main strategies proposed across the corpus for handling outlier weights/activations during quantization?
questions.answer: REPLACE: e.g. summarize 2-3 distinct strategies you found across multiple papers, and which papers propose each.
questions.notes: synthesis questions should draw on 2+ papers

questions.question: REPLACE: e.g. Do any papers disagree on whether per-channel or per-tensor quantization matters more at low bit-widths?
questions.answer: REPLACE with the actual disagreement you found, naming both papers/positions.
questions.notes: only include real contradictions you found while reading -- don't manufacture these

questions.question: How did weight-only quantization methods evolve from 8-bit to sub-4-bit approaches between roughly 2021 and 2025?
questions.answer: REPLACE with a short chronological account, naming the key papers/methods at each step.

questions.question: REPLACE: ask about a specific technique/model family that your corpus does NOT cover.
questions.answer: insufficient evidence -- this corpus does not contain papers addressing this.
questions.notes: correct system behavior is to abstain, not guess. Track this separately in scoring.
